children: Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Tourism has announced updates to four regulations governing travel and tourism services, tour guiding, hospitality facilities, and private hospitality units, as part of efforts to modernise the Kingdom’s tourism regulatory framework and improve the visitor experience.

The ministry said the reforms aim to enhance operational efficiency, align regulations with evolving business models and international best practices, and incorporate feedback from investors, operators, and beneficiaries while protecting tourist rights.
Under the travel and tourism services regulation, licensing categories have been simplified, operational flexibility expanded, and different license-duration options introduced.
The revised rules also clarify service providers’ rights and obligations.

Tour guiding regulations streamline classification categories, allowing guides to work across multiple regions and disciplines. They also establish clearer licensing and qualification requirements and permit direct bookings and contracts between guides and tourists.
For hospitality facilities, the updates strengthen licensing, classification, digital integration, and online booking and payment standards.
New specialised accommodation categories have also been introduced, with classifications linked directly to quality and safety compliance.
Meanwhile, private hospitality units will move from a permit-based system to a formal licensing system, with requirements covering safety, property eligibility, and consumer protection.
Ministry spokesperson Nasr Alansari said the reforms establish clear quality benchmarks, supported by training programs to strengthen sector capabilities and help operators achieve compliance.
The ministry said the updated regulations and compliance guidelines are available through its official portal. Operators and investors can seek assistance through the Unified Tourism Centre at 930.

title: ZAWYA: Saudi Arabia updates tourism regulations to modernise sector
